quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals.
Use proper lane positions.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible, signal your turns, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, watch for hazards, and be ready for changes in driving conditions.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a green arrow or signal that lets you turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear immediately.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.
Relax and steer straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over uneven bridge gratings, simply relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: What is true about operating a motorized scooter?

options.text: You can only operate it during the day.
You do not need a driver license.
You can use any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can use any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot and the driver cannot see you. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" — sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel is not tightened properly to the frame.
The front tire hit an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When holding the handlebars, your arms should be:

options.text: Bent sharply at the elbow.
Slightly bent.
Fully extended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly bent.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Slightly bent arms reduce fatigue and let you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: In areas where hazards may exist, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Keep the same speed.
Assume everything is safe.
Position their hands over the clutch and brake levers to react quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position their hands over the clutch and brake levers to react quickly.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, slow down. Keep your hands ready over the clutch and both brake levers so you can react fast in an emergency.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: Both lean in the same direction.
They lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays more upright to balance.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, your steering will suddenly feel:

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If your steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: Before turning, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Stop the engine power from changing during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the engine power from changing during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. If you shift gears while turning, the power to the rear wheel can suddenly change and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it slowly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with extra weight takes longer to stop and speed up. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when carrying a passenger than when you are alone.

questions.question: High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes:

options.text: Can be used by motorcyclists.
Can be used by motorcyclists, but only on weekends.
Cannot be used by motorcyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used by motorcyclists.
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, motorcyclists are allowed to use HOV lanes at any time, even if there is only one rider.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothes with reflective material to be seen better, even in daylight. Always wear long sleeves and pants to protect your arms and legs.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light, especially when the tail light is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Blocks most of your vision.
Allows you to see as much to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Can be dangerous to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see as much to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A helmet does not limit your vision. Any U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will let you see everything you need to ride safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right
Left
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space possible. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider look for in a protective jacket?

options.text: Black or another dark color.
Warmth.
Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows you to move freely. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Ignore the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: If it is safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Continue to apply the front brake.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it firmly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake right away and then re-apply it firmly. Use both front and rear brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to avoid hazards like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have the most space around you.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a borrowed motorcycle?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway immediately.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all controls are. Practice riding in a controlled area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: What type of clothing should you wear when riding?

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing to be more visible, even during the day. Reflective materials also help increase your visibility.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles will correctly judge your speed and location.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what is true about the mirrors?

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Like any vehicle, motorcycle mirrors have blind spots. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
